items.title: Google Drive MCP
items.text:
A Go MCP server that exposes Google Drive, Docs, and Sheets operations as tools over stdio transport.

Sheets is the primary use case — the server is formula-aware, handles multi-tab workbooks, and supports safe writes that don't clobber adjacent formulas.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Google Drive — list, search, upload, download, move, and delete files
  • Google Sheets — read/write ranges, append rows, batch operations across tabs, formula-safe writes
  • Google Docs — create, read, append, and find-and-replace text
  • OAuth2 authentication — browser-based consent flow with automatic token caching and refresh

items.title: Quick Start
items.text:
1. Set up a Google Cloud project with Drive, Sheets, and Docs APIs enabled
  2. Install the binary with go build
  3. Configure credentials and run the first-time auth flow
  4. Add the server to your MCP client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, etc.)

items.title: What is this?
items.text:
googledrive-mcp is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server written in Go. It gives AI assistants like Claude the ability to interact with your Google Drive, Sheets, and Docs through a standardized tool interface.

When connected to an MCP client, the server exposes tools that let Claude:

  • Browse and search your Google Drive
  • Read and write spreadsheet data (with full formula support)
  • Create and edit Google Docs
  • Upload and download files

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Go 1.21 or later — Install Go
  • A Google account — with access to Google Drive
  • A Google Cloud project — free tier is sufficient (see Google Cloud Setup)

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
The server uses stdio transport, meaning it communicates with MCP clients through standard input/output. This is the simplest and most common MCP transport.

MCP Client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, etc.)
    ↕ stdio
googledrive-mcp binary
    ↕ HTTPS
Google APIs (Drive v3, Sheets v4, Docs v1)

Authentication uses OAuth2 with a desktop application flow. On first run, the server opens your browser for Google consent. After authorization, tokens are cached locally and refreshed automatically.

items.title: Next Steps
items.text:
1. Create a Google Cloud project and download credentials
  2. Build the binary
  3. Configure and authenticate
  4. Connect to your MCP client

items.title: Credentials File
items.text:
The server reads OAuth2 client credentials from:

~/.config/googledrive-ai/credentials.json

This file is the JSON you downloaded from Google Cloud Console during Google Cloud Setup. If the file is missing, the server prints setup instructions and exits.

items.title: First-Run Authentication
items.text:
On first run, the server performs a browser-based OAuth2 consent flow:

  1. The server starts a temporary local HTTP server on a random port
  2. Your default browser opens to Google's consent screen
  3. Sign in and grant the requested permissions (Drive, Sheets, Docs)
  4. The browser redirects back to the local server with an authorization code
  5. The server exchanges the code for access and refresh tokens
  6. Tokens are saved to ~/.config/googledrive-ai/token.json

If the browser doesn't open automatically, the server prints a URL to stderr that you can copy and paste.

items.title: Token Caching
items.text:
After initial authorization, the server uses cached tokens from:

~/.config/googledrive-ai/token.json
  • Tokens are refreshed automatically when they expire
  • Refreshed tokens are saved back to disk
  • You should not need to re-authorize unless you revoke access or delete the token file

items.title: Re-Authenticating
items.text:
If you need to re-authorize (e.g., changed scopes or revoked access):

rm ~/.config/googledrive-ai/token.json

The next time the server starts, it will prompt for authorization again.

items.title: File Permissions
items.text:
The server creates config files with restricted permissions:

  • token.json is written with 0600 (owner read/write only)
  • The config directory is created with 0700 (owner access only)

items.title: Google Cloud Setup
items.text: This guide walks you through creating a Google Cloud project and obtaining OAuth2 credentials for the MCP server.

items.title: 1. Create a Google Cloud Project
items.text:
1. Go to the Google Cloud Console
  2. Click the project dropdown at the top of the page
  3. Click New Project
  4. Enter a project name (e.g., "Google Drive MCP")
  5. Click Create

items.title: 2. Enable APIs
items.text:
Enable the three APIs the server needs:

  1. Go to APIs & Services > Library
  2. Search for and enable each of these:
  3. Google Drive API
  4. Google Sheets API
  5. Google Docs API

Alternatively, use the direct links:

  • Enable Drive API
  • Enable Sheets API
  • Enable Docs API

items.title: 3. Configure OAuth Consent Screen
items.text:
1. Go to APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen
  2. Select External user type (or Internal if using Google Workspace)
  3. Fill in the required fields:
  4. App name: Google Drive MCP
  5. User support email: your email
  6. Developer contact: your email
  7. Click Save and Continue
  8. On the Scopes page, click Add or Remove Scopes and add:
  9. https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive
  10. https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets
  11. https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents
  12. Click Save and Continue
  13. On the Test users page, add your Google account email
  14. Click Save and Continue

items.title: 4. Create OAuth2 Credentials
items.text:
1. Go to APIs & Services > Credentials
  2. Click Create Credentials > OAuth client ID
  3. Select Desktop app as the application type
  4. Enter a name (e.g., "googledrive-mcp")
  5. Click Create
  6. Click Download JSON to download the credentials file

items.title: 5. Save the Credentials File
items.text:
Move the downloaded file to the configuration directory:

mkdir -p ~/.config/googledrive-ai
mv ~/Downloads/client_secret_*.json ~/.config/googledrive-ai/credentials.json

The server expects the file at ~/.config/googledrive-ai/credentials.json.

items.title: Build from Source
items.text:
Clone the repository and build the binary:

git clone https://github.com/pariwork/googledrive-ai.git
cd googledrive-ai
go build ./cmd/googledrive-mcp

This produces a googledrive-mcp binary in the project root.

items.title: Verify the Build
items.text:
Check that the binary was created:

ls -la googledrive-mcp

The binary communicates over stdio, so running it directly will appear to hang (it's waiting for MCP protocol messages on stdin). You'll connect it to an MCP client in the MCP Client Setup step.

items.title: Install to PATH (Optional)
items.text:
To make the binary available system-wide:

go install ./cmd/googledrive-mcp

This installs to $GOPATH/bin (usually ~/go/bin). Make sure this directory is in your PATH.

items.title: MCP Client Setup
items.text: Connect the Google Drive MCP server to your preferred MCP client.

items.title: Claude Code
items.text:
Add the server using the CLI:

claude mcp add googledrive-mcp /path/to/googledrive-mcp

Or if you installed it to your PATH:

claude mcp add googledrive-mcp googledrive-mcp

The server will be available in your next Claude Code session.

items.title: Claude Desktop
items.text:
Edit the Claude Desktop configuration file:

  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
  • Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json

Add the server to the mcpServers section:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "googledrive-mcp": {
      "command": "/path/to/googledrive-mcp"
    }
  }
}

Restart Claude Desktop to pick up the change.

items.title: Other MCP Clients
items.text:
The server uses stdio transport, which is supported by all MCP clients. The general pattern is:

  1. Point the client to the googledrive-mcp binary path
  2. Set transport to stdio
  3. No additional arguments or environment variables are required

The server handles authentication on first run via the browser flow described in Configuration.

items.title: Docs Tools
items.text: Tools for creating and editing Google Docs. These provide a simplified interface focused on common text operations.

items.title: docs_create
items.text:
Create a new Google Doc.

Parameter Type Required Description title string Yes Document title content string No Initial text content

Example:

{
  "name": "docs_create",
  "arguments": {
    "title": "Meeting Notes - June 2026",
    "content": "## Attendees\n\n## Agenda\n\n## Action Items\n"
  }
}

Returns the new document ID.

items.title: docs_read
items.text:
Read the full text content of a document.

Parameter Type Required Description document_id string Yes The document ID

Example:

{
  "name": "docs_read",
  "arguments": {
    "document_id": "1a2b3c4d5e"
  }
}

items.title: docs_append
items.text:
Append text to the end of a document.

Parameter Type Required Description document_id string Yes The document ID text string Yes Text to append

Example:

{
  "name": "docs_append",
  "arguments": {
    "document_id": "1a2b3c4d5e",
    "text": "\n\n## Follow-up\n\nSchedule review meeting for next week."
  }
}

items.title: docs_replace
items.text:
Find and replace text within a document.

Parameter Type Required Description document_id string Yes The document ID find_text string Yes Text to search for replace_text string Yes Replacement text

Example:

{
  "name": "docs_replace",
  "arguments": {
    "document_id": "1a2b3c4d5e",
    "find_text": "DRAFT",
    "replace_text": "FINAL"
  }
}

items.title: Drive Tools
items.text: Tools for managing files and folders in Google Drive.

items.title: drive_list
items.text:
List files and folders in a directory.

Parameter Type Required Description folder_id string No Folder ID to list. Defaults to root ("My Drive") page_size integer No Maximum number of results to return

Example:

{
  "name": "drive_list",
  "arguments": {
    "folder_id": "1a2b3c4d5e",
    "page_size": 20
  }
}

items.title: drive_search
items.text:
Search Drive by name, type, or content.

Parameter Type Required Description query string Yes Search query (name, type, or content) page_size integer No Maximum number of results to return

Example:

{
  "name": "drive_search",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "budget 2026",
    "page_size": 10
  }
}

items.title: drive_get
items.text:
Get metadata for a specific file.

Parameter Type Required Description file_id string Yes The file ID

Example:

{
  "name": "drive_get",
  "arguments": {
    "file_id": "1a2b3c4d5e"
  }
}

items.title: drive_create_folder
items.text:
Create a new folder.

Parameter Type Required Description name string Yes Folder name parent_id string No Parent folder ID. Defaults to root

Example:

{
  "name": "drive_create_folder",
  "arguments": {
    "name": "Project Reports",
    "parent_id": "1a2b3c4d5e"
  }
}

items.title: drive_upload
items.text:
Upload a file to Drive.

Parameter Type Required Description name string Yes File name in Drive file_path string Yes Local path of the file to upload parent_id string No Parent folder ID. Defaults to root

Example:

{
  "name": "drive_upload",
  "arguments": {
    "name": "report.pdf",
    "file_path": "/tmp/report.pdf",
    "parent_id": "1a2b3c4d5e"
  }
}

items.title: drive_download
items.text:
Download a file's content.

Parameter Type Required Description file_id string Yes The file ID to download

Example:

{
  "name": "drive_download",
  "arguments": {
    "file_id": "1a2b3c4d5e"
  }
}

items.title: drive_delete
items.text:
Move a file or folder to the trash.

Parameter Type Required Description file_id string Yes The file ID to delete

Example:

{
  "name": "drive_delete",
  "arguments": {
    "file_id": "1a2b3c4d5e"
  }
}

items.title: drive_move
items.text:
Move a file to a different folder.

Parameter Type Required Description file_id string Yes The file ID to move new_parent_id string Yes Destination folder ID

Example:

{
  "name": "drive_move",
  "arguments": {
    "file_id": "1a2b3c4d5e",
    "new_parent_id": "6f7g8h9i0j"
  }
}

items.title: Sheets Tools
items.text: Tools for reading and writing Google Sheets. Sheets is the primary use case for this server — all write operations are formula-safe and use USER_ENTERED input mode so formulas are interpreted correctly.

items.title: sheets_list_sheets
items.text:
List all tabs (sheets) in a spreadsheet with their dimensions.

Parameter Type Required Description spreadsheet_id string Yes The spreadsheet ID

Example:

{
  "name": "sheets_list_sheets",
  "arguments": {
    "spreadsheet_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms"
  }
}

items.title: sheets_get_metadata
items.text:
Get spreadsheet metadata including named ranges, sheet properties, and dimensions.

Parameter Type Required Description spreadsheet_id string Yes The spreadsheet ID

Example:

{
  "name": "sheets_get_metadata",
  "arguments": {
    "spreadsheet_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms"
  }
}

items.title: sheets_read_range
items.text:
Read a range of cells from a specific tab.

Parameter Type Required Description spreadsheet_id string Yes The spreadsheet ID range string Yes A1 notation range (e.g., Sheet1!A1:D10) render_option string No "formatted" (default) for display values, "formula" for raw formulas

Example — read formatted values:

{
  "name": "sheets_read_range",
  "arguments": {
    "spreadsheet_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms",
    "range": "Sheet1!A1:D10"
  }
}

Example — read formulas:

{
  "name": "sheets_read_range",
  "arguments": {
    "spreadsheet_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms",
    "range": "Sheet1!A1:D10",
    "render_option": "formula"
  }
}

items.title: sheets_create
items.text:
Create a new spreadsheet.

Parameter Type Required Description title string Yes Spreadsheet title sheet_names string[] No Names for initial tabs. Defaults to one tab named "Sheet1"

Example:

{
  "name": "sheets_create",
  "arguments": {
    "title": "Q3 Budget",
    "sheet_names": ["Summary", "Revenue", "Expenses"]
  }
}

Returns the new spreadsheet ID.

items.title: sheets_add_sheet
items.text:
Add a new tab to an existing spreadsheet.

Parameter Type Required Description spreadsheet_id string Yes The spreadsheet ID sheet_name string Yes Name for the new tab

Example:

{
  "name": "sheets_add_sheet",
  "arguments": {
    "spreadsheet_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms",
    "sheet_name": "Q4 Forecast"
  }
}

items.title: sheets_write_range
items.text:
Write values to a specific range. Uses USER_ENTERED input mode — formulas like =SUM(A1:A10) are interpreted, not stored as text.

Parameter Type Required Description spreadsheet_id string Yes The spreadsheet ID range string Yes A1 notation range (e.g., Sheet1!A1:C3) values any[][] Yes 2D array of values to write

Example:

{
  "name": "sheets_write_range",
  "arguments": {
    "spreadsheet_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms",
    "range": "Sheet1!A1:C2",
    "values": [
      ["Item", "Quantity", "Total"],
      ["Widgets", 100, "=B2*5.99"]
    ]
  }
}

items.title: sheets_append_rows
items.text:
Append rows after the last row of data on a tab. Automatically finds the end of existing data.

Parameter Type Required Description spreadsheet_id string Yes The spreadsheet ID sheet_name string Yes Tab name to append to values any[][] Yes 2D array of rows to append

Example:

{
  "name": "sheets_append_rows",
  "arguments": {
    "spreadsheet_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms",
    "sheet_name": "Sheet1",
    "values": [
      ["Gadgets", 50, "=B3*12.99"],
      ["Sprockets", 200, "=B4*3.49"]
    ]
  }
}

items.title: sheets_batch_update
items.text:
Perform multiple read and write operations in a single call. Useful for working across multiple tabs in one request.

Parameter Type Required Description spreadsheet_id string Yes The spreadsheet ID reads object[] No Array of ranges to read writes object[] No Array of range/values pairs to write

Example:

{
  "name": "sheets_batch_update",
  "arguments": {
    "spreadsheet_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms",
    "reads": [
      { "range": "Revenue!A1:D10" },
      { "range": "Expenses!A1:D10" }
    ],
    "writes": [
      {
        "range": "Summary!A1:B2",
        "values": [
          ["Category", "Total"],
          ["Revenue", "=Revenue!D10"]
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
